neighbours.label: the opening of a general rule or maxim about how things usually go (Every effort..., Sometimes..., you can't...)
fire: In this business, every mistake costs you a customer.
As my grandmother said, sometimes the quiet ones surprise you most.
Out on the farm, you can't rush a good harvest.
In the newsroom, every effort is made to check each quote.
On long trips, sometimes the detours are the best part.
Around here, you can't trust the weather in April.
For a beginner, every small win builds confidence.
In politics, you can't please everybody at once.
quiet: In this business, our office moved to Elm Street in March.
As my grandmother said, the bus to town left at noon.
Out on the farm, we finished the harvest on Tuesday.
In the newsroom, the editor printed the article at six.
On long trips, we packed sandwiches in a red cooler.
Around here, the bakery closes at four on weekdays.
For a beginner, the class meets in room twelve.
In politics, the vote was held on a rainy Thursday.

notes: Card mixes 'of', 'Every', 'Sometimes', 'take', "can't"; probe: 'Every effort was made' 0.45, 'Sometimes the best answer' 0.29, "You can't fool" 0.45, a plain report 0.17. Output suppresses ' usually', ' can', ' should', ' typically'. Near misses are specific one-off events.
